title: Orlando Travel Guide

hero.alt: Lake Eola and downtown Orlando skyline
hero.headline: Orlando Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: See Orlando as both a real Central Florida city and the hub of a much larger visitor region.

overview: See Orlando as both a real Central Florida city and the hub of a much larger visitor region.
Combine downtown neighborhoods, lakes, and springs with carefully identified resort-area excursions rather than calling every famous attraction a city attraction.

highlights.title: Orlando essentials
highlights.description: Use the destination's defining landscapes, neighborhoods, and cultural sites to structure the visit.

highlights.title: Outdoor access
highlights.description: Build in time for the water, parks, preserves, or trails that genuinely define Orlando.

highlights.title: Local context
highlights.description: Keep nearby municipalities and protected lands distinct so the itinerary stays geographically accurate.

highlights.title: Practical pacing
highlights.description: Group stops by area and leave room for weather, traffic, and seasonal conditions.

thingsToDo.title: Lake Eola Park and Downtown
thingsToDo.description: Use Lake Eola and the surrounding downtown streets as the orientation point for the incorporated City of Orlando.

thingsToDo.title: Mills 50 and Audubon Park
thingsToDo.description: Explore independent restaurants, murals, small businesses, and neighborhood-scale culture away from the resort corridor.

thingsToDo.title: Winter Park — a separate city
thingsToDo.description: Visit Park Avenue, museums, Rollins College, and the chain of lakes, while keeping Winter Park correctly identified as its own municipality.

thingsToDo.title: Greater Orlando theme parks
thingsToDo.description: Walt Disney World and other major resorts are part of the broader Orlando visitor region, not downtown Orlando; give them separate full-day blocks.

thingsToDo.title: Universal and International Drive area
thingsToDo.description: Treat the southwest tourism corridor as its own zone to avoid wasting time crossing between downtown and resort districts.

thingsToDo.title: Wekiwa Springs State Park
thingsToDo.description: Head north of Orlando for spring-fed water, paddling, trails, and natural Central Florida in a separately managed state park.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Cooler months are easiest for outdoor planning
bullets: Late fall through early spring generally brings lower humidity and comfortable outdoor conditions.
Summer is hot, humid, and storm-prone; start exposed activities early and keep afternoon plans flexible.
Busy winter and holiday periods reward advance reservations for popular tours and timed attractions.

travelTips: Group each day by geography instead of crossing the region repeatedly.
Use early mornings for exposed outdoor activities and waterfront time.
Check park, marine, and weather conditions before nature-focused plans.
Treat nearby municipalities and protected areas as separate destinations with their own access rules.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for Orlando?
faq.a: Two to three days is a good starting point for the core sights plus one outdoor or regional experience.

faq.q: Is Orlando good for outdoor travelers?
faq.a: Yes. The strongest itineraries combine the destination itself with nearby water, parks, preserves, or trails.
It depends on the destination, but a car or guided tour is often useful for protected lands and regional excursions.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: For high-demand wildlife, boating, park, and holiday-period experiences, advance booking is sensible.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Orlando is an incorporated Central Florida city within a much larger tourism region.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: The landscape is defined by lakes, wetlands, springs, and flat uplands; downtown lies well north of the Disney resort area.

sections.heading: History & culture
paragraphs: Downtown, Mills 50, Audubon Park, Ivanhoe Village, and nearby Winter Park reveal a local arts and dining culture beyond the parks.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: Wekiwa Springs and other spring systems show the region's natural hydrology, while the theme-park complexes are separate built destinations.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: Organize days by zone: downtown, Universal/I-Drive, Disney-area resorts, and springs each deserve their own travel block.
